data.headline: DIA’s long-end Treasury spread widened to 38 basis points
data.summary: The 30-year minus ten-year Treasury spread widened from 37 to 38 basis points on November 4, even as both yields declined. This matters when comparing different financing maturities for long-lived projects. Company credit spreads and project cash flows determine the final borrowing and investment decision.

bull.text: The 30-year benchmark fell from 5.32% to 5.28%, a 4-basis-point decline. The ten-year declined from 4.95% to 4.90%, or 5 basis points. Both Treasury benchmarks eased over the November 3–4 interval.

bear.text: The 30-year yield retained a 38-basis-point premium over the ten-year, up from 37. Longer financing terms therefore carried a wider Treasury maturity spread in this observation.

watch.text: October 27 Dow futures positions showed asset managers net long 12,233 contracts and leveraged funds net long 96. The leveraged category was close to balanced in that older weekly report.

limitations: These Treasury benchmarks cover different maturities. Actual Dow-company borrowing costs, new orders, capital spending and DIA returns remain unmeasured.
The futures figures describe the DJIA x $5 contract. They carry weekly reporting lag and provide no direct DIA fund-flow or options reading.
